transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-03 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Alex Marin, Priya Shah, Diego Ruiz (Redwood) — Maya Lin, Jonas Reed, Leah Porter (Cedarway)

Auto Summary: quick alignment on runbook and security; plan perf pilot; share docs and schedule follow-ups.

00:00 Alex: Hey team, thanks for joining. Alex from Redwood here, I'll run the top level agenda. Uh, quick check on timing — we've got 45, 47 minutes. Is that still good?
00:10 Maya: Yep that's fine. We have the core folks on — Jonas is on SecOps, Leah on product.
00:16 Jonas: Hello, yes. Sorry slight background — noisy day here.
00:20 Alex: No worries. Quick round — Priya from customer success, Diego our solution engineer, will jump in on the network and perf bits.
00:28 Priya: Hi all. Goal for today is to walk through the onboarding runbook, capture any Cedarway-specific constraints, and set next steps for the pilot.
00:40 Leah: Sounds great. We're particularly worried about data residency, key management, and the SLA for low-latency customer-facing calls.
00:50 Diego: Got it. We'll cover the private deployment options and also how Redwood Dedicated can be configured — sorry I always say Redwood Dedicate, that's my bad — but both dedicated and VPC-private options.
01:05 Maya: Can you also outline where credentials live? We currently require HSM-backed KMS for any PII processing, and we lock down egress.
01:15 Diego: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS — we integrate with AWS KMS or a partner HSM; for private deployments there's a bring-your-own-KMS flow. For hosted, we can do KMS integration with a customer key but there are policy steps.
01:30 Jonas: Importantly: Cedarway policy requires no model state or logs to persist in plaintext outside our tenancy and we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
01:40 Priya: We can map that to retention settings and audit log forwarding — Diego can show the runbook section on logs.
01:48 Diego: I'll pull that up — on the runbook we have a default retention of 30 days, but we can configure to retain zero tokens and forward metrics only. There are a few gotchas: prefix cache may store KV in memory for latency reasons, so we need to clear policies and runtime flags to avoid persistent cache if that's a blocker.
02:10 Leah: That cache comment — can you expand? If we turn off prefix caching doesn't that hurt latency for short sessions?
02:20 Diego: Yeah, it's a tradeoff. With continuous batching and KV caching we hit lower p99 latencies, but if policy forbids any cached prompt data we can put a TTL of 0 and rely on higher capacity to keep p95 within threshold. That's where Dedicated capacity helps.
02:40 Alex: Maybe high level: hosted is fastest to get started but less isolation, Dedicated gives capacity isolation and predictable throughput, Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you control for KMS/ingress/egress.
02:55 Maya: We're leaning toward Private in our compliant environments and maybe use hosted for non-PII internal tooling. Does that make sense?
03:05 Alex: Totally, that's a common pattern. For pilot we usually do a hybrid: pilot on a reserved Dedicated pool in our cloud region, while we work with infra to prep the private deployment timeline.
03:20 Jonas: Timeline — we have a security review next Tuesday, and we'd like to have an initial perf artifact to take to that meeting. Can you run a benchmark we can include?
03:30 Diego: Yes, we can run a small-batch perf test against a sample model and give you p50/p95/p99 and cost estimates. We'll need a short test prompt set and expected concurrency.
03:42 Maya: We can provide 50 representative prompts and target concurrency of 20 rps for the user facing API.
03:50 Diego: Great. Also want to flag model quantization — we can recommend quantized variants to cut cost, but there's an accuracy tradeoff; we'll include quality regressions in the report.
04:05 Leah: Who on the Redwood side is our single point of contact?
04:09 Priya: I'll be your CSM for onboarding; Alex will be commercial contact; Diego is SE for tech.
04:18 Leah: Perfect.
04:20 Alex: Let's go through the runbook sections — I'll read them out and you call out anything that doesn't map to your infra. Section one: access and SSO, Section two: networking, Section three: KMS and encryption, Section four: run stages and rollout, Section five: benchmarks and metrics.
04:40 Maya: On SSO: we use Okta SAML, and we require SCIM for provisioning. Can you support SCIM?
04:48 Priya: Yes we support SAML + SCIM for user provisioning — we've done the SSO runbook steps with other finance customers. We'll send the SAML metadata and SCIM schema.
05:00 Jonas: Network: we need to see the IP ranges for any outbound endpoints — also request for egress via our NAT only, no direct internet from the instance.
05:12 Diego: For Dedicated/Private we can either peer into your VPC or set up private endpoints — we have an allowlist of IPs for hosted control-plane callbacks. We'll provide the list.
05:25 Leah: Do you support keepalives through our proxy? We have a corporate proxy that terminates TLS.
05:32 Diego: Yes, we have proxy-friendly connectors, but for private deployments it's usually a straight VPC peering. We'll note proxy config in the runbook.
05:42 Alex: I'm going to capture those infra asks as action items — Jonas to share network diagram, Redwood to share IP allowlist.
05:50 Jonas: I'll get that by Monday.
05:52 Maya: Question on logging: we need to ship audit logs to Splunk — what's the output format?
06:00 Diego: JSON events with timestamp and request ids; we can push to your S3 and you can hook the S3 to Splunk, or we can forward via a secure syslog endpoint. We'll list options in the runbook.
06:15 Jonah: (laughs) Jonas — yes we'll pick S3.
06:20 Jonas: S3 option is fine if it's STS-accessed with our role.
06:24 Diego: Totally supported.
06:26 Maya: On KMS, our security team insists on HSM-backed keys. Any blockers?
06:32 Alex: For Private, none. For Dedicated there's a path to provide your KMS key and rotate keys. For hosted there are stricter controls and sometimes we need a hashed key flow; we'll share the exact security doc.
06:45 Leah: Ok great. Can you show the sample run stages?
06:50 Priya: Stage one is sandbox access for devs, stage two is pilot with limited user bucket and metrics, stage three is production rollout and scale. Each stage has acceptance criteria.
07:05 Maya: Acceptance criteria — we'd like <150ms p50 and p95 under 500ms for single-turn, plus error rate below 0.5%. Is that doable?
07:20 Diego: For single-turn with a 512 token model, on Dedicated we can often hit that p50, p95 might be close depending on concurrency and batching. We'll put a perf plan with target instance types and batching config.
07:35 Alex: Note that sequence length and response length matter; we can tune token limits to meet those latencies.
07:42 Leah: On cost — can you give us a very rough unit cost for the pilot? We need a ballpark for internal budgeting.
07:50 Alex: We'll send a pilot estimate: compute + tokens + storage. For Dedicated pilot with modest throughput expect a fixed monthly commit + variable token usage. We'll follow up with a draft pricing sheet.
08:05 Jonas: On compliance docs — can you provide SOC2 and the last pen test summary?
08:12 Priya: Yes we'll attach SOC2 and the recent red team summary; some redactions but enough for security review.
08:20 Maya: One more thing — we have regulatory needs around EU data residency for some customers; will that require a separate private deployment in eu-west?
08:30 Alex: We can route EU workload to an eu region and pin model serving there; for regulated workloads customers often choose Private in-region. We'll note options: region pinning, data residency controls, and model snapshot export restrictions.
08:45 Leah: Great.
08:46 Diego: Quick technical deep-dive note — if you plan to use streaming responses with function calling, that changes the runtime characteristics: more long-lived connections, different batching assumptions. We'll note guidance in the runbook.
09:00 Maya: We will use streaming for chat-based support flows.
09:04 Diego: Ok then we'll tune keepalive and connection limits accordingly.
09:10 Leah: Can you show an example of the onboarding checklist?
09:14 Priya: I'll read the checklist: 1) Admin SSO + SCIM configured, 2) network peering and IP allowlist confirmed, 3) KMS and key rotation policy agreed, 4) audit logging destination provisioned, 5) pilot prompt set and traffic profile provided, 6) perf window scheduled and run, 7) production rollout plan and rollback steps.
09:36 Maya: That maps well. I'd like to add a compliance sign-off task from our legal.
09:42 Priya: Added. We'll include owner fields.
09:46 Alex: Ok moving to pilot perf — Diego, what do you need from Cedarway to run the 20 rps 50-prompt test?
09:55 Diego: A CSV of prompts, representative headers, expected concurrency profile, and a test API key (we can use a scoped pilot key). We'll execute a few runs and share metrics and a perf spreadsheet.
10:10 Maya: We'll provide the prompts and a safe subset with no real PII for test.
10:16 Diego: Perfect. We'll also include a small quality evaluation using your metrics — e.g., precision on entity extraction if that's part of product.
10:25 Leah: Yes we need entity extraction quality included.
10:28 Diego: Noted.
10:30 Alex: Let's do a quick risk register — top risks I see: network complexity and firewall rules, KMS policy friction, and achieving latency SLOs at scale. Any others?
10:44 Jonas: Vendor lock-in concern from procurement — they want options to move models or use different runtime.
10:50 Alex: We can document export and rollback processes; Redwood supports model pinning and rollbacks, and we'll recommend multi-model fallback policies.
10:58 Leah: Ok.
11:00 Priya: Recap of action items and owners — Alex to share runbook v0.1, Diego to prepare perf plan and test harness, Jonas to share network diagram, Maya to confirm prompt set, and Priya to schedule the perf window.
11:20 Alex: Any final questions?
11:23 Maya: No, this was helpful.
11:25 Jonas: None from SecOps.
11:28 Leah: Thanks everyone.
11:30 Alex: Great. We'll target sending the runbook and docs by end of day Monday, and aim for the perf window the following week. Thanks all.

End transcript.

Notes: occasional transcription mismatches observed (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" instead of "Redwood Dedicated"). Some speaker labels simplified. Shared links during call: Runbook draft (link in follow-up), SOC2 pack (will be attached), sample perf spreadsheet (to be shared).
